judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 102. It would have made harassing a sports official a crime, at the lowest misdemeanor level. The rule applied when the harassment comes from the official's calls or their role as an official. The Pennsylvania House passed it 137-66. As of August 2026 the Senate had not voted on it.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 1042. It would have let state prisoners earn credit toward a shorter minimum sentence by finishing job training and school programs. It also set out sentencing and parole rules for second-degree murder, which now carries an automatic life sentence. The Pennsylvania House passed the final version 102-100. As of August 2026 the bill had not become law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 1045. It would have required school nurses and school staff who work directly with students to take seizure recognition and first aid training every three years, starting in the 2026-27 school year. That training is optional under current law. The Pennsylvania House passed it 130-71. As of August 2026 the Senate had not voted on it.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 1396. It would have changed the election code in several ways. Election workers would be paid at least $175 per election. Every county would have to provide at least two ballot drop boxes, and tell the state where they are at least 65 days before an election. The Pennsylvania House passed it 102-101. As of August 2026 the Senate had not voted on it.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 1574. It would have created a state loan fund. A redevelopment agency, or a land bank that takes over vacant property to get it back in use, could borrow up to $500,000 in startup money from the state. The Pennsylvania House passed it 160-42. As of August 2026 the Senate had not voted on it.

It would have made the education department publish guidance for students, parents and coaches on spotting the warning signs of mental health trouble. The health and human services departments would help write it. The Pennsylvania House passed it 107-94. As of August 2026 the Senate had not voted on it.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 2042. It would have extended the state's youth sports concussion rules to official recreational leagues. Those rules on managing concussions and head injuries now cover only school sports. The Pennsylvania House passed it 121-79. As of August 2026 the Senate had not voted on it.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 2189. It would have raised Pennsylvania's minimum wage above the $7.25 federal floor on a single statewide schedule: $11 an hour in 2027, $13 in 2028 and $15 after that. The state rate has been stuck at $7.15 since 2007. The Pennsylvania House passed it 104-95. As of August 2026 the Senate had not voted on it.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 2246. It would have let the Department of Environmental Protection regulate and require permits for water used or withdrawn by large data centers, meaning those using more than 100,000 gallons a day. The Pennsylvania House passed it 116-84. As of August 2026 the Senate had not voted on it.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 273. It would have let a county adopt its own property maintenance code, using a nationally recognized code or its own version, and appoint inspectors to enforce it, with fines for violations. It also created a state grant program, up to $100,000 a town with matching funds, to help towns with no code enforcement start one. Penalty money would feed a fund paying for demolition, cleanup and repair of blighted property. The Pennsylvania House passed it 110-93. As of August 2026 the Senate had not voted on it.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 441. It would have let the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources protect wild native land invertebrates, such as native insects, as protected species. The department would gather data on their populations, range and habitat. The Pennsylvania House passed it 102-101. As of August 2026 the Senate had not voted on it.

The Pennsylvania House passed it 102-101. As of August 2026 the Senate had not voted on it.

Current law requires each district to set out discipline for bullying and name a staff member to receive reports. The Pennsylvania House passed it 136-65. As of August 2026 the Senate had not voted on it.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for House Bill 846. The prevailing wage law sets minimum pay on public construction jobs. This bill would have widened it to cover HVAC duct cleaning and custom work built off site. It would also have banned split rates, where workers get different pay at different times on the same job. The Pennsylvania House passed it 126-76. As of August 2026 the Senate had not voted on it.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 1236. It would have let operators of construction sites disturbing between one and five acres apply to skip the federal clean water permit that such sites now need. The Pennsylvania Senate passed it 30-20. As of August 2026 the House had not voted on it.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 1400. Under current law, second-degree murder carries an automatic life sentence. That covers a death during another serious crime. This bill would have ended the automatic life term for defendants who were 18 or older, letting courts set a minimum prison term instead, so parole becomes possible. The Pennsylvania Senate passed it 30-20. As of August 2026 the House had not voted on it.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 490. It would have barred letting a defendant go free on a promise to appear, or on bail with no money down, once a judge finds the person is a threat to public safety. An arresting officer could not release such a person before taking them to a judge. The Pennsylvania Senate passed it 32-17. As of August 2026 the House had not voted on it.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 686. It would have made it a serious crime, at the lowest felony level, to deliberately change, destroy, hide or remove a public record that someone has requested under the state's open records law. The Pennsylvania Senate passed it 31-18. As of August 2026 the House had not voted on it.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 712. It would have tightened how abandoned oil and gas wells must be sealed, requiring a cement plug at least 50 feet long at the reachable bottom of the well, with the depth and effectiveness of the plug confirmed. The Pennsylvania Senate passed it 32-16. As of August 2026 the House had not voted on it.

judgments.yea_description: Voted for Senate Bill 908. The prevailing wage law sets minimum pay on public construction jobs. This bill would have narrowed it, so fixing up a home, school safety and security work, and HVAC duct cleaning would no longer count as public work covered by those pay rules. The Pennsylvania Senate passed it 37-13. As of August 2026 the House had not voted on it.
